run.question: Application-gateway server is returning 502 errors in the app-101 namespace. Please investigate.

report.summary: The alert names namespace app-101, but no namespace of that name exists in the queried cluster: the namespaces present are default, kube-node-lease, kube-public, kube-system, local-path-storage, opspilot-readonly and otel-demo, and the demo application workloads live in otel-demo. The only gateway-shaped workload there is Deployment frontend-proxy (ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.0.2-frontend-proxy, an Envoy proxy on container port 8080, exposed by NodePort Service frontend-proxy:8080). That deployment is at revision 1 (no rollout since its 2026-11-20T16:32:06Z creation), 1/1 ready, and every backend it is configured to talk to (frontend:8080, image-provider:8081, jaeger-query:16686, load-generator:8089, flagd:8013/8016) has a ready endpoint, so no upstream outage, crash, pending pod, node pressure or resource-quota exhaustion was observed in this cluster. Two configured upstream destinations do not exist at all in this cluster (grafana:80 and flagd port 4000, while the flagd container exposes only 8013 and 8016), which is a plausible source of 502 responses on those routes but remains a hypothesis. Critically, no observation of any 502 itself could be obtained for this Run: all Prometheus and Jaeger tools returned source errors and pod log reads returned zero lines, so neither the error rate, error spans, nor gateway access logs are known. No root cause can be named from the available evidence.

claims.text: No namespace named app-101 exists in the cluster; the seven namespaces returned are default, kube-node-lease, kube-public, kube-system, local-path-storage, opspilot-readonly and otel-demo.

The only gateway-like workload in the cluster is Deployment frontend-proxy in namespace otel-demo (container frontend-proxy, image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.0.2-frontend-proxy, containerPort 8080/service), exposed by Service frontend-proxy of type NodePort on port 8080.
Deployment frontend-proxy is at deployment revision 1 (created 2026-11-20T16:32:06Z) with 1 ready/1 available/1 updated replica, i.e. its pod template has not been rolled since install.

The frontend-proxy container environment sets GRAFANA_HOST=grafana, GRAFANA_PORT=80, FLAGD_UI_HOST=flagd, FLAGD_UI_PORT=4000 alongside FRONTEND_HOST=frontend/FRONTEND_PORT=8080, IMAGE_PROVIDER_HOST=image-provider/8081, JAEGER_HOST=jaeger-query/16686 and LOCUST_WEB_HOST=load-generator/8089.
No Service named grafana exists in any namespace (29 services enumerated cluster-wide, none named grafana) and no Deployment named grafana exists in otel-demo (21 deployments listed).

The flagd container declares only container ports 8013 (name rpc) and 8016 (name ofrep), and Service flagd exposes only ports 8013 and 8016 — port 4000, which frontend-proxy is configured to use as FLAGD_UI_PORT, is not exposed by the flagd pod or Service.

Every upstream endpoint the gateway is configured to reach that does exist has a ready address: frontend 8080, image-provider 8081, jaeger-query 16685/16686, load-generator 8089, flagd 8013/8016, and frontend-proxy itself 8080, each with one address in the Endpoints object.
All 31 otel-demo-and-system pods listed are in phase Running with Ready conditions True, including frontend-proxy-844799bcdb-pv5mn, frontend-6c9bc688bf-58jmw and every demo service pod.

Containers of frontend-proxy-844799bcdb-pv5mn and of 17 other otel-demo pods share one last-termination instant of 2026-11-21T04:23:42Z with exitCode 255 and reason Unknown; the pods are running now with no OOMKilled or Evicted state recorded, so this was a node/runtime-wide container restart rather than per-pod damage.
Node opspilot-m1-control-plane is Ready (true since 2026-11-20T16:32:02Z) with MemoryPressure, DiskPressure and PIDPressure all False.

The in-cluster Prometheus alerting rule file (ConfigMap prometheus, key alerting_rules.yml) defines only CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh and the two OpsPilot self alerts (OpsPilotAgentAbsent, OpsPilotModelCallsFailing); it contains no rule about 502 responses or an application gateway.

All eleven flags in ConfigMap flagd-config (demo.flagd.json) are in state ENABLED with defaultVariant off, e.g. productCatalogFailure, cartFailure, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, adFailure, imageSlowLoad — no declared fault variant is switched on in the stored configuration.

The 502 responses attributed to the gateway may come from frontend-proxy routes whose configured upstream destinations do not exist in this cluster: grafana:80 (no grafana Service or Deployment anywhere) and flagd:4000 (flagd exposes only 8013/8016), i.e. a configuration mismatch carried in Deployment frontend-proxy's environment. This is unverified because the Envoy route table is baked into the image and neither Envoy access logs nor gateway metrics were readable in this Run.

The reported 502s may belong to a different environment than the cluster queried, because the alert's namespace app-101 does not exist here and the only gateway in this cluster is frontend-proxy in otel-demo; mapping the alert's 'application-gateway' to frontend-proxy is an inference from topology, not from error evidence at that entity.

No upstream outage, crash loop, pending pod or endpoint shortage was observed for the gateway or its backends: all demo pods are Running/Ready, all six listed gateway-relevant Services have one ready endpoint, and the node reports no pressure — so a simple 'upstream is down' explanation is not supported by any observation in this Run.

frontend-proxy's pod template is unchanged (deployment revision 1) and the stored flagd configuration has every fault flag at defaultVariant off, so no applied rollout or declared fault-injection flag was found on the gateway path; flagd's runtime overrides at incident time are not readable.

Resource exhaustion (OOMKill, eviction, node memory/disk/PID pressure) as the cause of gateway failures is rejected: no container reports OOMKilled, no pod is Evicted or Failed, all pods are Running/Ready, and the node's MemoryPressure, DiskPressure and PIDPressure conditions are False.

Restore telemetry access and then read the gateway's own signals: Envoy access logs/upstream-502 counters per route from frontend-proxy-844799bcdb-pv5mn and HTTP 5xx series for service frontend-proxy, to establish whether the 502s are on /grafana and /feature (the routes pointing at absent grafana:80 and flagd:4000) or on the / frontend route.

Confirm with the alert source which cluster/namespace 'app-101' and 'application-gateway' refer to; if it is this cluster, either deploy the missing grafana upstream or remove the GRAFANA_HOST/GRAFANA_PORT route, and align FLAGD_UI_PORT with a port flagd actually serves (8013/8016), after verifying the intended route table.

gaps: No metric evidence exists for this Run: metrics_range_query, execute_prometheus_instant_query, get_metric_names, get_all_labels and get_prometheus_target all returned status error with reason SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE (attempted 2026-11-21T07:03:33Z–07:04:34Z), so 502 counts, HTTP 5xx ratios and kube-state-metrics series for frontend-proxy are unknown, not zero.

No trace evidence exists for this Run: traces_search, traces_list_services and traces_list_operations all returned status error with reason SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so frontend-proxy error spans and downstream span statuses are unknown.

Application logs are unavailable: fetch_pod_logs returned zero lines (no_data) for frontend-proxy-844799bcdb-pv5mn, frontend-6c9bc688bf-58jmw, load-generator-5ff476786d-xg5nz and prometheus-readonly-proxy-f4866f767-62bgn for 2026-11-21T06:03:26Z–07:03:26Z, including previous container instances; the gateway's own error lines therefore could not be read.

The events query across all namespaces for the authorized window returned zero events, so no Scheduled/Started/Unhealthy/kill evidence is available to date the 04:23:42Z container-restart wave or any later gateway event; why every otel-demo container terminated at that instant is unknown.
The ingresses query returned an empty list, so any external host/path routing into the gateway is unknown; the networkpolicies and resourcequotas queries also returned empty lists.

The Envoy configuration of frontend-proxy is built into the image and was not readable, so which paths are routed to grafana:80 and flagd:4000 (and whether those routes carry real traffic) is unknown; the prometheus-readonly-proxy configuration is in a Secret that cannot be read.
The effective flagd flag values at incident time (runtime overrides on top of the ConfigMap defaults, all 'off') are unknown; no flag was seen being switched.
The alert's own subject could not be located: no namespace app-101 and no object named application-gateway exist in the queried cluster, so the alert may describe a different environment.

The change_history integration is not integrated, so changes such as the 2026-11-21T04:23:42Z cluster-wide container restarts and the otel-collector/prometheus revision-2 rollouts cannot be attributed to a specific actor or time.
next_steps: Restore or re-point the Prometheus and Jaeger data sources, then re-query error rates and error spans for service frontend-proxy and operation-level 502s before drawing any conclusion about the gateway.
Read frontend-proxy access/error logs (or scrape its /stats upstream 5xx counters) to see which route produces the 502s and whether the upstream is refused, reset or timing out.
Verify the intended Envoy route table for /grafana and /feature routes and either add the missing grafana upstream or remove/repair those routes.
Confirm with the alerting system whether app-101/application-gateway refers to this cluster; if not, investigate the actual cluster before acting here.

content:
groups:
- name: opspilot-lab
  rules:
  - alert: CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh
    annotations:
      description: '{{ $value | humanizePercentage }} of checkout PlaceOrder server
        spans ended in error over the last 5 minutes.'
      summary: checkout PlaceOrder error ratio above 50%
    expr: |
      label_replace(label_replace(
        (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[5m])))
        /
        (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder"}[5m])))
      , "namespace", "$1", "k8s_namespace_name", "(.*)"), "service", "$1", "service_name", "(.*)")
      > 0.5
    for: 2m
    labels:
      cluster: opspilot-m1
      opspilot_integration_id: m0-otel-20260909
      severity: critical
- name: opspilot-self
  rules:
  - alert: OpsPilotAgentAbsent
    annotations:
      description: role {{ $labels.role }} ({{ $labels.instance }}) has not answered
        /metrics for 2 minutes.
      summary: an OpsPilot health listener is down or the worker is not scraped
    expr: up{job="opspilot"} == 0 or absent(up{job="opspilot",role="worker"})
    for: 2m
    labels:
      opspilot_self: "true"
      severity: critical
  - alert: OpsPilotModelCallsFailing
    annotations:
      description: '{{ $value }} consecutive model calls failed on {{ $labels.instance
        }}.'
      summary: OpsPilot model calls are failing
    expr: opspilot_model_consecutive_failures >= 2
    for: 1m
    labels:
      opspilot_self: "true"
      severity: critical
